gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histopathologically confirmed, based on biopsy or surgical resection, glioblastoma or WHO grade 4 astrocytoma, IDH-mutant

candidate_evidence.quote: Concurrent chemoradiation with temozolomide (TMZ) over 3 weeks (40 Gy in 15 fractions). The gross tumor volume (GTV) plus margin will be boosted simultaneously (SIB) to 52.5 Gy in 15 fractions.
In this trial, we will examine the outcomes of increased radiation dose, combined with reduced-margin adaptive radiotherapy in this patient population.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Biopsy or surgical resection performed ≤ 6 weeks prior to study entry

role_evidence.quote: Concurrent dose-escalated chemoradiation with temozolomide (TMZ) on the MR-Linac with weekly adaptation

The usual standard of care for patients over 65 diagnosed with glioblastoma ("GBM") or Grade 4 astrocytoma, IDH-mutant is a 3-week course of radiotherapy, with concurrent and adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ).

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent, GBM standard of care

coder_notes: Radiotherapy trial (dose-escalated, reduced-margin adaptive MR-Linac RT) in elderly GBM or IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma; temozolomide is standard concurrent backbone, not the question. Exclusion reason could alternatively be established_therapy_only. cns5_terminology: conditions use 'Glioblastoma Multiforme' and list 'Glioblastoma, IDH-mutant' (historical); no IDH-wildtype requirement, though the record separately names WHO grade 4 astrocytoma, IDH-mutant. IDH mentioned only as an allowed histology, not as an entry requirement, so not listed as a biomarker. Gadolinium contrast mentioned only in eligibility for MRI; not a registered intervention, not listed.
